hero.title: Your types were always the contract. Now they're enforced.
hero.subtitle: TS Typed instruments the TypeScript you already wrote to validate your data at runtime — no duplicate schema, no decorator-per-field, no drift between what your types say and what your code actually checks.

cta.title: Your TypeScript can do more.
cta.body: Start with a plain TypeScript, Express, or NestJS project and keep safety explicit at every boundary.

features.eyebrow: A safety layer, not another schema
features.heading: The contract that follows your code
features.intro: Validation, value objects, and safe errors connected to the TypeScript your team already maintains.

noSchema.title: No schema duplication
noSchema.body: Your existing TypeScript types ARE the runtime contract. Nothing else to keep in sync.

valueObject.title: Auto-constructed value types
valueObject.body: Declare a field as CPF, Email, or your own ValueObject — a raw value crossing that boundary becomes a validated instance automatically.

nestjs.title: NestJS integration
nestjs.body: A ready-made exception filter maps violations to safe HTTP responses, with per-field custom messages and entity/DTO disambiguation.

validators.title: Validators package
validators.body: Email, CPF, CNPJ, and more — real validation logic, not just string types.

safeErrors.title: Safe by default
safeErrors.body: StrictTypeError never leaks the raw value or a stack trace to a client.

opensource.title: Open source
opensource.body: Apache-2.0, on GitHub, built in the open.

example.title: See it in action
example.body: No decorators scattered across your model. The compiler finds boundaries and keeps the contract visible in code.
